$$

q-70319.worked_solution:
We multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{2y}\cdot \frac{6{y}^{2}}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot 6{y}^{2}}{2y\cdot {x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{6{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}{2{x}^{2}y} \\  & =3y\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In the above example, we performed some cancellations after multiplying. However, with more complex expressions, it's often easier to cancel *before* multiplying.

q-3517.worked_solution:
First, we cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator of one fraction and a denominator of the other one. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{11p{q}^{2}}{{r}^{3}}\cdot \frac{5{r}^{2}}{121{p}^{4}q} & =\frac{11pq\cdot q}{r\cdot {r}^{2}}\cdot \frac{5\cdot {r}^{2}}{11pq\cdot 11{p}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{11pq}\cdot q}{r\cdot \cancel{{r}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{5\cdot \cancel{{r}^{2}}}{\cancel{11pq}\cdot 11{p}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{q}{r}\cdot \frac{5}{11{p}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{5q}{11{p}^{3}r}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8

Which of the following is equivalent to x2−16x2−5x+6⋅x−3x−4?

a
x−4x−3
b
x+4x−2
c
2x+1x−2
d
x+42x−1
e
x−8x−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we factor all of the expressions and cancel any terms that appear in both a numerator and a denominator. Then, we multiply the numerators and the denominators as follows:

x2−16x2−5x+6⋅x−3x−4=(x+4)(x−4)(x−2)(x−3)⋅x−3x−4=(x+4)(x−4)(x−2)(x−3)⋅(x−3)x−4=x+4x−2
